items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The manager of the Savoy, a Mr. Charles Buchanan, the owner of the place, a Mr. Moe Gale and his father, came out of their office to see what all the shouting was about

ctx.x: We composed a number and called "Lawd Lawd" and decided to really break it one Sunday at the Savoy. Frank Newton sang the words and we answered him repeating the same words. Frank scatted the middle part and there were not other words except "Lawd Lawd". We played it on the second set alternating with Fess Williams and it went over so big with the crowd that it was the only number we played on that set. The people kept shouting Lawd Lawd ever time we finished it. And when we came back on the stand again, it was…

The manager of the Savoy, a Mr. Charles Buchanan, the owner of the place, a Mr. Moe Gale and his father, came out of their office to see what all the shouting was about and everyone was so enthusiastic about "Lawd Lawd" that it was the only number we played for the rest of the two hours that we were there. And that really tied up the contract for our coming engagement at the Savoy.

Playing the numbers was one of the biggest and best paying rackets in New York City. Gangsters had complete control of the racket and they also controlled the bootleg alcohol racket and controlled most of the bars. Almost everybody played the numbers from one penny to dollars. For one cent it paid 5 dollars so that even the poorest of the poor had a chance. The last three numbers of the total amount of the result of the days receipt of the stock market were the winning numbers. Bob Sawyer taught me how to play…
